questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: A postposition forces the oblique form, and बेटा changes to बेटे.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: A masculine noun in -ा must change to -े before a postposition.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: For more than one son the plural oblique बेटों is needed, not the singular oblique बेटे.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The verb agrees with चाय, which is singular. बेटे here is one son, not several.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: घर does not end in -ा, so there is no -े form for it to take.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: There is no postposition here, so the noun stays in its direct form.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: कुत्ता ends in -ा, so it takes the oblique कुत्ते before a postposition.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: If more than one room is meant, the noun needs the plural oblique कमरों.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: If several dogs are meant, the plural oblique कुत्तों is required — the singular form does not cover both.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: If more than one house is meant, the plural oblique घरों is needed — the unchanged form covers only the singular.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: -ें is a feminine plural ending. A masculine plural before a postposition takes -ों, whatever the noun's origin.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: -े is what a final -ा becomes. आदमी ends in -ी, so there is nothing for that ending to attach to.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The long ी cannot take -ों directly. It shortens to ि and a य appears between the vowels.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: लड़के is the oblique of लड़का, which is a different word meaning boy. लड़की does not change at all.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: A long ी cannot carry -ों directly. It shortens to ि and takes a य before the ending.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: दिन is masculine, so its plural before a postposition is दिनों. दिनें is not a form Hindi has.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The -े ending exists only for Class 1 nouns ending in -ा. भाई does not qualify.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The long ई shortens to इ before the य. Keeping it long is the single most common misspelling of this word.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: बेटे is the oblique of बेटा. If you mean the daughter, the form is बेटी, unchanged.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The long ी shortens to ि before the य. This is the same trap as भाईयों and हाथीयों.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: -े is what a Class 1 masculine ending in -ा turns into. किताब is feminine and ends in a consonant, so it takes no ending in the singular.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The य and the shortened vowel belong to nouns ending in a long -ी. किताब ends in a consonant, so -ों attaches directly.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: को governs both nouns, so बेटा must go oblique even though it is not the word sitting directly in front of the postposition.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: कुत्ता replaces its -ा rather than adding to it, and बिल्ली shortens its -ी rather than keeping it.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The noun does not change, so the adjective is the only thing that can mark the oblique — and it must.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: रात is feminine and ends in a consonant. There is no -े form for it to take.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: There is no vowel here for a य to bridge. The ending goes straight onto the consonant.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: Getting the first noun right does not carry over. लड़की still needs its vowel shortened and a य added.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The -े ending exists only for nouns ending in -ा. Neither of these words qualifies, so neither changes.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: शहर cannot show the oblique, so the adjective has to. Leaving it as छोटा makes the phrase unmarked.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: -े is the masculine oblique ending. A feminine noun takes बड़ी whatever follows it.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: Getting the noun right does not excuse the adjective. Both are marked and both have to move.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: Pronouns never stand beside को. मैं and को fuse into मुझे.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The pronoun and the postposition merge. तुम को leaves them standing apart.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: वह has no oblique form of its own. The pronoun is replaced by the stem उस, and को fuses onto it.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: Making the noun plural does not change its gender. किताब is feminine in every number, so the adjective stays बड़ी.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: चाय is feminine, which is exactly why Module 4 asked you to memorise it. The masculine oblique -े never applies here.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: से fuses with the oblique stem just as को does. The two words are never written apart.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: आप takes no ending of its own. The postposition attaches to it unchanged.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: वे has no oblique form. The stem उन supplies the possessive उनके, and वे disappears entirely.
